plan: Eight new items (meticulous WIC, literary final-sentence function, two-part data claim, conservators vs critic cross-text, its, past perfect progressive, restatement transition, method synthesis) plus S020-03 and S020-08 relabelled easy.

passages.title: Field notebooks
passages.text: The botanist's field notebooks were ______: every measurement was dated, labeled, and cross-referenced to the photograph of the plant it described.

passages.title: The second sentence
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
Mara had rehearsed the speech all week. When the principal finally called her name, she walked to the microphone and found that the first sentence had vanished from her memory. She looked out at the rows of folding chairs. Then she began with the second sentence, and no one ever knew.

passages.title: Library loans
passages.text:
A town library recorded the number of print and e-book loans each year.
Year | Print loans | E-book loans
2019 | 900 | 100
2020 | 600 | 400
2021 | 700 | 450
2022 | 750 | 500
A librarian claims that after a sharp drop in 2020, print loans partly recovered in the following years.

passages.title: Bare canvas (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A critic argues that the bare patches of canvas in the painter's late works show that she was too ill to finish them, and that the paintings should be displayed with a note calling them incomplete.

Text 2
Conservators examining the late paintings with infrared imaging found detailed underdrawings that outline the bare patches precisely, along with the painter's written notes marking those areas "leave open."

passages.title: Reading room
passages.text: After a year of construction, the library opened a new ______ section with low shelves, beanbag chairs, and a small stage for story hours.

passages.title: Stone mill
passages.text: Built in 1854 to grind wheat for the valley's farms, the stone mill on Fuller Creek ______ a pottery studio and a small gallery.

passages.title: Island power
passages.text: Most of the island's electricity comes from wind turbines and solar panels; only about a tenth is generated by burning fuel. ______ roughly nine-tenths of the island's power is renewable.

passages.title: Water hole cameras
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers placed motion-sensing cameras at 40 water holes in a national park.
• The cameras recorded animal visits for 12 months.
• Elephants visited the water holes at night more often during the dry season.
• The researchers suggest that night visits help elephants avoid the heat.

passages.title: Gym survey
passages.text: A survey of the members of a large gym found that 80 percent of them exercise at least four times a week. A city official cited this result as evidence that most of the city's residents exercise frequently. However, ______

passages.title: A revised date
passages.text: For decades, archaeologists dated a hilltop fort to about 500 BCE, relying on the style of pottery found inside its walls. Recently, a team used radiocarbon dating on charcoal from the fort's earliest hearths and obtained dates near 800 BCE. The team argues that the pottery style must have remained in use for far longer than previously assumed.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: every measurement was dated, labeled, and cross-referenced
candidates.explanation: Dating, labeling, and cross-referencing every measurement shows great care: "meticulous."

A.rationale: "Sporadic" means irregular or occasional; every measurement was recorded.

C.rationale: "Cryptic" means hard to understand; careful labels make the notes clear.

D.rationale: "Extravagant" means excessive or showy; nothing suggests excess.

hints: What do the details after the colon show about the notebooks?
candidates.remember: The words after a colon often define the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It suggests that Mara's speech was poorly received by the audience.
choices.B: It explains why Mara forgot the first sentence of her speech.
choices.C: It shows that Mara had never rehearsed the opening of her speech.
choices.D: It reveals that Mara recovered from her lapse without anyone noticing.

candidates.evidence: Then she began with the second sentence, and no one ever knew.
candidates.explanation: The final sentence resolves the tension: Mara skipped the forgotten line, and "no one ever knew," so the audience never noticed.

A.rationale: Nothing indicates how the audience received the speech.

B.rationale: The sentence describes what she did next, not why she forgot.

C.rationale: The text says she rehearsed all week.

hints: What problem does the final sentence resolve?

strategy.explanation: Identify the tension before the final sentence.

candidates.remember: A final sentence often resolves the tension the text builds.

candidates.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the librarian's claim?

choices.A: Print loans fell from 900 in 2019 to 600 in 2020, then rose to 750 by 2022.
choices.B: E-book loans rose every year, from 100 in 2019 to 500 in 2022.
choices.C: Total loans were 1,000 in 2019 and 1,250 in 2022.

candidates.evidence: after a sharp drop in 2020, print loans partly recovered
candidates.explanation: The claim has two parts: a drop in 2020 and a partial recovery. A shows the drop (900 to 600) and the rise to 750, which is still below 900.

B.rationale: This concerns e-books, not the recovery of print loans.

C.rationale: Totals combine both formats and do not show what happened to print loans.

D.rationale: A single year cannot show both the drop and the partial recovery.

hints: The claim has two parts. Which choice covers both?

strategy.explanation: Split the claim into its parts and check each choice.

candidates.remember: Evidence must cover every part of the claim.

candidates.stem: Based on the texts, how would the conservators in Text 2 most likely respond to the critic's claim in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that the paintings should be labeled as incomplete
choices.B: By claiming that the painter was never ill during her later years
choices.C: By arguing that the bare patches were planned rather than left unfinished
choices.D: By questioning whether infrared imaging can reveal underdrawings

candidates.evidence: the painter's written notes marking those areas "leave open."
candidates.explanation: Underdrawings outlining the bare patches and notes saying "leave open" show the patches were deliberate, contradicting the critic's view that they are unfinished.

A.rationale: The conservators' evidence suggests the bare areas were intended.

B.rationale: Text 2 says nothing about the painter's health.

D.rationale: The conservators rely on infrared imaging; they do not question it.

hints: What do the notes "leave open" suggest?

strategy.explanation: Find the evidence in Text 2 that bears on Text 1's claim.

candidates.remember: Ask what the second text's evidence implies about the first text's claim.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: low shelves, beanbag chairs, and a small stage for story hours
candidates.explanation: "Children" is an irregular plural that does not end in s, so its possessive is "children's."

B.rationale: "Children" is already plural, so the possessive adds 's, not s'.

C.rationale: "Childrens" is not a word, and it lacks an apostrophe to show possession.

D.rationale: Without an apostrophe, the word does not show that the section is for children.

strategy.explanation: Form the plural first, then add the possessive.

candidates.remember: Irregular plurals not ending in s take 's.

candidates.subskill: Finite verb after an introductory modifier
candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.evidence: the stone mill on Fuller Creek
candidates.explanation: The introductory phrase "Built in 1854 ..." modifies "the stone mill," which needs a main verb: "now houses."

A.rationale: "Housing" is not a finite verb, so the sentence would have no main verb.

B.rationale: "Which now houses" turns the rest into a clause, leaving "the stone mill" without a main verb.

C.rationale: "Having housed" is a participle, not a main verb.

hints: Does the sentence have a main verb without the blank?

strategy.explanation: Eliminate choices that leave the sentence without a finite verb.

candidates.remember: Every sentence needs a subject and a finite verb.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: only about a tenth is generated by burning fuel
candidates.explanation: If only a tenth comes from fuel, nine-tenths is renewable: the second sentence restates the first, so "In other words" fits.

A.rationale: The second sentence agrees with the first; it does not contrast with it.

B.rationale: The second sentence restates the first in different terms; it is not an example.

D.rationale: "Even so" signals something surprising in spite of the first sentence, but the second follows directly from it.

hints: Does the second sentence add new information or restate the first?
candidates.remember: Use "in other words" when a sentence restates the previous one.

candidates.stem: The student wants to describe the study's method. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The researchers used motion-sensing cameras at 40 water holes to record animal visits for 12 months.
choices.B: Elephants visited the park's water holes at night more often during the dry season, the researchers found.
choices.C: The researchers suggest that elephants visit water holes at night to avoid the heat of the day.
choices.D: In a national park, elephants changed when they visited water holes depending on the season.

candidates.evidence: Researchers placed motion-sensing cameras at 40 water holes
candidates.explanation: A method describes how the study was done: cameras at 40 water holes, recording for 12 months. Only A gives that.

B.rationale: This reports a finding, not the method.

C.rationale: This gives the researchers' explanation, not the method.

D.rationale: This summarizes a result, not how the study was done.

hints: What is a method, as opposed to a finding?

strategy.explanation: Look for how the data were collected.

candidates.remember: A method is how the data were gathered, not what was found.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the survey found that some gym members exercise fewer than four times a week.
choices.B: the gym is one of the largest in the city and has members of many ages.
choices.C: frequent exercise has been shown to improve health in many studies.
choices.D: gym members are likely to exercise more often than city residents in general.

candidates.evidence: A city official cited this result as evidence that most of the city's residents exercise frequently.
candidates.explanation: "However" signals a flaw in the official's reasoning. Gym members are not a representative sample of residents: they are probably more active than average.

A.rationale: That 20 percent exercise less does not undermine the official's conclusion about residents.

B.rationale: Size and age variety do not fix the problem that all respondents chose to join a gym.

C.rationale: This is about the benefits of exercise, not about whether the survey represents residents.

hints: Who was surveyed, and who is the conclusion about?

strategy.explanation: Compare the sample with the group in the conclusion.

candidates.remember: A conclusion about a group needs a sample that represents that group.
candidates.revision_note: S020-03 resubmitted unchanged in content and relabelled easy: both blind solvers rated it easy (70%).

candidates.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes a method for dating sites, explains its limits, and recommends that archaeologists abandon it.
choices.B: It gives an established date, reports conflicting evidence, and then offers an explanation for the conflict.
choices.C: It compares two forts, describes how each was dated, and concludes that they were built at the same time.
choices.D: It reports a new date for a fort and then gives evidence from pottery that confirms the new date.

candidates.evidence: The team argues that the pottery style must have remained in use for far longer than previously assumed.
candidates.explanation: Sentence 1 gives the old date, sentence 2 gives conflicting radiocarbon evidence, and sentence 3 explains the conflict by proposing that the pottery style lasted longer.

A.rationale: The team does not recommend abandoning pottery dating; it reinterprets how long a style lasted.

D.rationale: The pottery evidence supported the old date; the team explains why it misled.

hints: What does each of the three sentences do?

strategy.explanation: Label each sentence's role, then match.
